pr_body: Closes #15200 Hard code context windows for the most popular models. In the future we should probably allow overriding this via settings or determining it dynamically via API. Depending on hardware, users may wish to increase their timeout when work : ``` "language_models": { "ollama": { "low_speed_timeout_in_seconds": 120 } ``` Release Notes: - Added support for Ollama models with context length >2048.

issue_context.title: Requesting ability to set max_tokens for ollama models
issue_context.body: ### Check for existing issues - [X] Completed ### Describe the feature There doesn't seem to be any way to set the `max_tokens` for an ollama assistant model with the 0.147.0 nightly I'm using. I've attempted to set it in the config in a variety of ways and none of them had any visible impact in the UI. I always see "_n_ / 2k" in the top right corner, no matter which model I select. ### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help present your vision of the feature
comments: I was also quite surprised to see it being set to 2k as a limit. At first I thought I may have misconfigured my model, tried just llama3.18b and no dice, swapped to gemma2:27b and still was stuck at 2k. This was with num_ctx set as well.

@notpeter I love what you've done with #16877 but I would disagree that what's implemented there closes this; it's great to stop using 2048 as the default but this issue as filed is about _allowing the user to specify the context size_, and you're currently hardcoding the returned context size based on model name. (Thanks for reopening!)
Understood. I mostly implemented #16877 as a stop the bleeding solution to support >2048 tokens in models where it's possible.  I can understand the desire for explicit control over this value too.

Thank you @notpeter for even the stopgap solution, I'm gonna have to switch over to nightlies to give it a go!

Edit: Ah yea, I need to be able to explicitly set the token limit :/
FYI Zed Preview will have it tomorrow. Stable in a week.

You might want to add a "display_name" to your available models object to better differentiate.  I believe we ask ollama to list available models, but because I don't think they expose an API method to determine the custom `num_ctx` for a model specified in a Modelfile -- instead we have a hard coded list in the code for common models, with a default of 2048. So the two models are one sourced from the list (2048) and one from your `available_models` in settings.

https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/d3b46fd2f82abd6af851497980a4e378fe258228/crates/ollama/src/ollama.rs#L73-L89

review_comments: Rad, I think this is great.
It's going to be slightly wrong still as the tokenization is different between many of these models and tiktoken itself. However, it's a good estimate for the user.
The estimates are still fuzzy, but previously our requests was including `num_ctx` 2048 which caused ollama to prematurely truncate context there.
Oh yikes, I didn't realize this was truncating it! I thought it was just our estimate for the window. Thank you!
